name: ebitda_l3_reinvestment_matched
mechanism: EV/EBITDA is a capitalized cash-flow multiple, so firms in the same 3-digit industry share risk, but within an industry the multiple still varies with growth, the return earned on reinvestment (ROIC), and how much of EBITDA is consumed by capex. Matching peers on capex intensity, growth and ROIC inside the industry should pick firms whose EBITDA converts to free cash flow and grows at similar rates, so they should carry similar multiples.
prediction: Median |ln(V_est/V)| below the L3/L2 industry median baseline (0.333) and beats it in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank capex_intensity 1, sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Matching on growth, ROIC and capex intensity inside the 3-digit industry is a sensible EBITDA-to-free-cash-flow argument, the rank features carry it out, and the year-by-year prediction against a named baseline can be tested.

name: ebitda_l4_size_harmonic
mechanism: The narrowest industry definition gives peers with the most similar products, customers and cyclicality, and similar size proxies for similar business risk and liquidity. The harmonic mean of multiples equals averaging earnings yields, which is less dominated by a few peers with temporarily depressed EBITDA and very high multiples, a known source of upward bias with the arithmetic mean.
prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median baseline on median error in at least 3 of 4 years, with lower mean error than 0.513.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l4 | rank log_sales 1, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=6, harmonic_mean, min_peers=4 | fallback [same industry_l3] -> [same industry_l2]
critic_reason: Narrowest SIC with size matching is a classic, sensible comps mechanism, the L4->L3->L2 fallback and size ranking carry it out, and the harmonic mean is correctly argued to limit upward bias; next time, explain in the mechanism why sales_growth_1y is in the ranking too.
note: explore re-graded 2026-11-04: the original score came from a name-keyed estimate cache (see grader.estimate)

name: ebitda_cross_industry_fundamentals
mechanism: Valuation theory says EV/EBITDA depends on growth, profitability of reinvestment, reinvestment needs, intangible investment and leverage-related risk, not on the SIC code itself. Picking the nearest firms across all industries on these drivers is a nonparametric version of the warranted-multiple approach that avoids imposing a linear functional form, and a trimmed mean guards against outlier peers.
prediction: Beats the Bhojraj-Lee warranted-multiple peers baseline (0.380) in at least 3 of 4 years, but does not beat the L3/L2 industry median overall.
compact: EV/EBITDA | rank roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 1, rnd_intensity 0.5, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=20, trimmed_mean, min_peers=3
critic_reason: Cross-industry nearest neighbours on value drivers is a distinct, theory-based idea (a nonparametric warranted multiple) that the recipe carries out, and the prediction can be tested; be aware that requiring rnd_intensity drops candidates without R&D data and may shrink or skew the 'all industries' pool.

name: sales_l2_margin_matched
mechanism: EV/Sales is approximately EBITDA margin times EV/EBITDA, so margin differences explain most of the spread in sales multiples even inside an industry. Restricting to the 2-digit sector keeps risk and cyclicality broadly similar while giving enough candidates to find peers with nearly the same EBITDA and gross margin and similar growth.
prediction: Median error below the L3/L2 industry median EV/Sales baseline (0.603) in all 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 3, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, median, min_peers=5 | fallback []
critic_reason: The EV/Sales = EBITDA margin x EV/EBITDA identity makes margin-heavy matching inside the 2-digit sector a specific, sensible mechanism, the weights match it, and 'all 4 years' is a sharp, testable claim.

name: sales_margin_band_cross_industry
mechanism: Because a dollar of sales is worth roughly the cash margin it produces capitalized at a growth-adjusted rate, firms with nearly the same EBITDA margin should have similar EV/Sales regardless of industry. A hard margin band enforces this, and ranking within the band on growth, gross margin and capex intensity matches the remaining drivers (growth and how much of the margin is eaten by reinvestment).
prediction: Beats the L3/L2 industry median EV/Sales baseline on median error in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=8 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.06]
critic_reason: A hard EBITDA-margin band across industries carries out the margin-capitalization argument directly, ranking within the band on growth and reinvestment covers the remaining drivers, and the prediction can be tested; note that the argument is weakest for firms with negative or near-zero margins.

name: sales_l3_margin_band_harmonic
mechanism: Combining the same 3-digit industry (shared risk and business model) with a margin band (shared cash conversion of sales) targets the two main determinants of the sales multiple at once. Within that set, gross margin, growth and R&D intensity capture pricing power and intangible investment, and the harmonic mean limits the influence of high-multiple peers.
prediction: Median error below 0.55 and lower than the L3/L2 industry median EV/Sales baseline in at least 3 of 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l3, band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 0.5 | k=6, harmonic_mean, min_peers=3 | fallback [same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.05] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.03]
critic_reason: Combining the industry screen with a margin band targets both risk and cash conversion, which is a new idea compared with proposals 3 and 4 alone, the screens, fallbacks and harmonic mean match the mechanism, and both prediction thresholds can be tested.

name: g02-01 EBITDA sector drivers with D&A wedge
mechanism: EBITDA ignores depreciation, so two firms with the same EBITDA margin but different EBIT margins differ in how much of EBITDA is consumed by asset replacement and how much is taxable; matching both ebitda_margin and ebit_margin implicitly matches D&A intensity. Doing this inside the 2-digit sector (shared macro risk and cost of capital) while also matching ROIC, growth and leverage combines the industry anchor with the driver-based nearest-neighbour idea, and a trimmed mean limits outlier peers.
prediction: Median error below the L3 industry median (0.333) and beats it in at least 3 of 4 years, with mean error below 0.50.

spec.name: g02-01 EBITDA sector drivers with D&A wedge

compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2 | rank ebitda_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=12, trimmed_mean, min_peers=6 | fallback []
critic_reason: Jointly matching EBITDA and EBIT margin is a new, coherent way to proxy D&A intensity, which is economically linked to EV/EBITDA, and the 2-digit sector anchor with this driver set is a genuinely new combination with a falsifiable yearly benchmark.

name: g02-02 EBITDA growth band cross-industry
mechanism: In a growing-perpetuity view the EV/EBITDA multiple is most sensitive to expected growth, so a hard band on recent sales growth forces peers into the same growth regime regardless of SIC code. Within that band, ROIC, capex intensity and R&D intensity determine how much of EBITDA must be reinvested to deliver the growth, and size proxies for risk, so the nearest firms on these should share the multiple.
prediction: Median error at or below 0.335 and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years with coverage above 95%.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen band sales_growth_1y±0.08 | rank roic 1, capex_intensity 1, rnd_intensity 1, log_assets 0.5, ebitda_margin 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=8 | fallback [band sales_growth_1y±0.16] -> []
critic_reason: A hard cross-industry band on sales growth is a new screen that directly implements the growth-regime mechanism, and ranking on reinvestment drivers (ROIC, capex, R&D) within it is consistent; note that 1-year growth is a noisy proxy for expected growth, which is exactly what the test will reveal.

name: g02-03 EBITDA transitory-margin peers in L3
mechanism: A large part of cross-sectional EV/EBITDA variation within an industry comes from transitory EBITDA: firms with temporarily depressed margins trade at high multiples because the market capitalizes normalized, not current, earnings. Matching within the 3-digit industry on EBITDA margin, net margin and ROE identifies firms at a similar point relative to normal profitability, so their multiples embed similar mean-reversion expectations.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with the largest gain among firms whose EBITDA margin is far from their industry's typical level.

spec.name: g02-03 EBITDA transitory-margin peers in L3

compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank ebitda_margin 1.5, net_margin 1, roe 0.5, sales_growth_1y 0.5 | k=7, median, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: The mechanism is about margins that are temporarily depressed relative to a firm's own normal level, but the recipe only matches current-level margins and ROE, which cannot tell a transitory dip apart from a structurally low-margin firm; it needs a feature that captures deviation or change (e.g. growth-history or margin-change signals) to implement the idea.
reason: critic: The mechanism is about margins that are temporarily depressed relative to a firm's own normal level, but the recipe only matches current-level margins and ROE, which cannot tell a transitory dip apart from a structurally low-margin firm; it needs a feature that captures deviation or change (e.g. growth-history or margin-change signals) to implement the idea.

name: g02-04 Sales economic-margin band (R&D add-back)
mechanism: Expensed R&D depresses reported EBITDA margin even though it is an investment, so R&D-heavy firms carry higher EV/Sales than their EBITDA margin suggests. Banding on EBITDA margin and then ranking on R&D intensity matches the economic (pre-R&D) margin, while growth, ROIC and capex intensity match the remaining capitalization and reinvestment drivers of the sales multiple.
prediction: Median error below 0.40 and beats the industry median in 4 of 4 years, with the biggest improvement over g01-05 in R&D-intensive firms.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.04 | rank rnd_intensity 1.5, sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 0.5 | k=12, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.08] -> []
critic_reason: Banding on EBITDA margin and then ranking heavily on R&D intensity is a specific implementation of matching pre-R&D economic margin, a new economic idea relative to g01-05/g01-06, with a falsifiable subgroup prediction for R&D-intensive firms.

name: g02-05 Sales soft-margin neighbours full coverage
mechanism: EV/Sales is approximately EBITDA margin times EV/EBITDA, so the dominant matching variable is margin, but a hard band loses firms; a heavily weighted soft distance on EBITDA and EBIT margin keeps full coverage while still forcing close margin matches. Secondary weights on growth, capex intensity and ROIC match the EV/EBITDA component (growth and reinvestment efficiency), across all industries.
prediction: Median error below 0.42 with coverage at least 99%, beating the industry median in 4 of 4 years.

spec.name: g02-05 Sales soft-margin neighbours full coverage

compact: EV/Sales | rank ebitda_margin 4, ebit_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, capex_intensity 1, roic 1 | k=10, median, min_peers=3
critic_reason: Replacing the industry screen with a heavily weighted soft margin distance plus EBIT margin, capex intensity and ROIC follows directly from the EV/Sales = margin x EV/EBITDA identity and adds new features and a new no-screen design, not a trivial variant of g01-04.

name: g02-06 Sales gross-margin band with operating leverage
mechanism: Gross margin reflects pricing power and business model (software vs. distribution), which sets the long-run attainable operating margin; firms in the same gross-margin band but with lower current EBITDA margin are often scaling and are valued on future margins. Banding on gross margin and ranking on EBITDA margin, growth and size matches both the business-model ceiling and the current position toward it.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years with median error below 0.45 and coverage above 90%.

spec.name: g02-06 Sales gross-margin band with operating leverage

compact: EV/Sales | screen band gross_margin±0.05 | rank ebitda_margin 2, sales_growth_1y 1, log_sales 0.5, asset_turnover 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band gross_margin±0.1] -> []
critic_reason: A gross-margin band as a business-model ceiling with ranking on current EBITDA margin, growth, size and asset turnover is a new screen and economic idea that the recipe implements faithfully, and the yearly-beat and coverage prediction is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_sector_growth_regime
mechanism: In a growing-perpetuity view EV/EBITDA is roughly (1 - reinvestment rate)/(WACC - g), so peers need both the same discount rate and the same growth regime. A 2-digit sector screen anchors cost of capital and cyclicality, a hard growth band puts peers in the same growth regime, and ranking on EBITDA and EBIT margins, ROIC and capex intensity matches how much of EBITDA must be reinvested to deliver that growth.
prediction: EV/EBITDA median error below the industry-median baseline (0.333) in at least 3 of 4 exploration years, with pooled median at or below 0.325.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band sales_growth_1y±0.1 | rank ebitda_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, roic 1, capex_intensity 1 | k=10, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Using growth as a hard screen inside the 2-digit sector, then ranking on reinvestment proxies (EBIT vs EBITDA margin, ROIC, capex intensity), follows the (1 - reinvestment)/(WACC - g) logic and is a real change from g02-01, which only ranked on growth; the prediction is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_leverage_capacity_band
mechanism: Lenders extend debt as a multiple of EBITDA in proportion to how stable and durable they judge that EBITDA to be, so a firm's net debt/EBITDA is an accounting-based revealed signal of the risk of its cash flows, which is the denominator of the EV/EBITDA multiple. Banding on net debt/EBITDA groups firms with similar perceived cash-flow risk and capital structure across industries, and ranking on ROIC, growth, EBIT margin, size and R&D matches the remaining value drivers.
prediction: Beats the industry-median EV/EBITDA baseline in at least 3 of 4 exploration years with full or near-full coverage (>95%).
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen band net_debt_to_ebitda±1 | rank roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1, ebit_margin 1, log_assets 1, rnd_intensity 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=8 | fallback [band net_debt_to_ebitda±2] -> []
critic_reason: A hard band on net debt/EBITDA is a new screen. It is accounting-only, and it is economically linked to EV/EBITDA both as a debt-market signal of cash-flow risk and because net debt/EBITDA is mechanically part of EV/EBITDA; the coverage and year-count prediction is falsifiable.

name: ebitda_value_chain_position
mechanism: Within a 3-digit industry, firms differ in where they sit on the value chain: branded or proprietary producers have high gross margins and low asset turnover, while commodity processors and distributors have thin margins and fast turnover, and these positions carry different durability of EBITDA and hence different multiples. Matching gross margin, asset turnover and EBIT margin inside the industry, plus growth, picks peers with the same business model rather than just the same product code.
prediction: EV/EBITDA pooled median error below 0.333 and beats the industry-median baseline in at least 3 of 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l3 | rank gross_margin 1, asset_turnover 1, ebit_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=8, trimmed_mean, min_peers=5 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Matching business model (gross margin vs asset turnover) inside the 3-digit industry is a new economic idea, not used in g01-01 or g02-03, and the rank features implement it directly; the prediction is falsifiable.

name: sales_margin_growth_grid
mechanism: EV/Sales is approximately the cash margin of a dollar of sales times a growth-dependent capitalization factor, so the two first-order drivers are margin and growth. A joint hard band on EBITDA margin and sales growth matches both factors directly across industries, and ranking on capex intensity, R&D intensity, ROIC and size matches reinvestment needs and risk, with fallbacks that relax growth first because margin matters most for the sales multiple.
prediction: EV/Sales pooled median error below 0.40 and beats the industry-median baseline (0.603) in 4 of 4 exploration years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.04, band sales_growth_1y±0.1 | rank capex_intensity 1, rnd_intensity 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08] -> []
critic_reason: The joint hard band on margin and growth turns EV/Sales = margin x growth-capitalization into a new two-way screen rather than ranking on growth as g02-04 did, the fallbacks are ordered to match the mechanism, and the prediction is falsifiable.

name: sales_ebit_margin_band
mechanism: Depreciation and amortization approximate the reinvestment needed to sustain the asset base, so EBIT margin is closer than EBITDA margin to the sustainable free-cash margin per dollar of sales that the sales multiple capitalizes. Banding on EBIT margin and then ranking on EBITDA margin (which jointly pins down D&A intensity), gross margin, growth and R&D intensity matches cash conversion, pricing power and expensed intangible investment.
prediction: EV/Sales beats the industry-median baseline in 4 of 4 exploration years with pooled median error below 0.42.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebit_margin±0.03 | rank ebitda_margin 1, gross_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 1 | k=12, trimmed_mean, min_peers=6 | fallback [band ebit_margin±0.06] -> []
critic_reason: Banding on EBIT margin as the sustainable free-cash margin, with EBITDA margin in the ranking to pin down D&A intensity, is a new screen variable and a coherent reason to expect similar sales multiples; the prediction is falsifiable.

name: sales_sector_risk_margin_band
mechanism: A cross-industry EBITDA-margin band matches the cash conversion of sales, but leftover error comes from different discount rates and cyclicality across sectors, which change the multiple applied to that margin. Requiring the same broad 2-digit sector inside the margin band anchors the discount rate while keeping enough candidates, ranking on growth, gross margin, capex intensity and debt-to-assets matches the remaining drivers, and falling back to the pure margin band keeps coverage when the sector is thin.
prediction: EV/Sales pooled median error below 0.39 and beats the industry-median baseline in 4 of 4 exploration years, with coverage above 90%.
compact: EV/Sales | screen same industry_l2, band ebitda_margin±0.04 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, capex_intensity 1, debt_to_assets 0.5 | k=8, median, min_peers=4 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08] -> []
critic_reason: This is essentially g01-06 with its own first fallback (same industry_l2 plus an EBITDA-margin band) promoted to the primary screen; the 'sector anchors the discount rate inside a margin band' idea was already tested there, and the 0.5-weight debt_to_assets addition is not tied to a distinct mechanism, so propose a genuinely new driver instead.
reason: critic: This is essentially g01-06 with its own first fallback (same industry_l2 plus an EBITDA-margin band) promoted to the primary screen; the 'sector anchors the discount rate inside a margin band' idea was already tested there, and the 0.5-weight debt_to_assets addition is not tied to a distinct mechanism, so propose a genuinely new driver instead.

name: sector_rnd_matched_ebitda
mechanism: R&D is expensed, so R&D-heavy firms report EBITDA that understates their economic (pre-investment) earnings and therefore carry systematically higher EV/EBITDA than low-R&D firms in the same sector. Hard-matching R&D intensity inside the 2-digit sector removes this accounting distortion while keeping shared macro risk, and ranking on EBITDA and EBIT margins (which jointly pin down D&A intensity), growth and ROIC matches the remaining value drivers.
prediction: Beats the industry median (L3, fallback L2) in at least 3 of 4 years with median error at or below 0.325, and improves most for firms with R&D intensity above 5%.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band rnd_intensity±0.03 | rank ebitda_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1, roic 1 | k=12, trimmed_mean, min_peers=6 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: Hard-matching R&D intensity within the 2-digit sector is a new screen with a clear accounting reason (expensed R&D makes EBITDA too low and the multiple too high), the margin, growth and ROIC ranking fits the stated drivers, and the R&D-above-5% subgroup claim makes it falsifiable.

name: size_band_driver_ebitda
mechanism: Firm size is a robust accounting proxy for cost of capital: small firms face higher discount rates, illiquidity and less durable cash flows, so they trade at lower EV/EBITDA than large firms with identical operating drivers. Banding on total assets puts peers in the same size/discount-rate class across industries, and ranking on ROIC, growth, EBIT margin, capex intensity and leverage matches the numerator drivers of the capitalized cash-flow multiple.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years and has median error below 0.335, with the gain concentrated in the smallest size quintile.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen band log_assets±0.75 | rank roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1, ebit_margin 1, capex_intensity 1, net_debt_to_ebitda 0.5 | k=15, median, min_peers=8 | fallback [band log_assets±1.5] -> []
critic_reason: A hard size band across industries is a screen not yet tried (earlier recipes only ranked on size), the size and cost-of-capital argument is economically sensible, the ROIC, growth, margin, capex and leverage ranking matches the stated numerator drivers, and the claim about the smallest size quintile is testable.

name: yield_averaging_growth_peers_ebitda
mechanism: In a growing-perpetuity model the EBITDA yield (EBITDA/EV) is approximately linear in (WACC - g)/(1 - reinvestment rate), whereas the multiple is convex in growth, so averaging peers' yields (the harmonic mean of multiples) is the less biased aggregator when peers differ slightly in growth. Selecting a broad set of cross-industry neighbours weighted most heavily on growth, and then on EBITDA/EBIT margins and ROIC (which pin down reinvestment needs), gives a large, driver-matched sample on which this yield averaging is effective.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years with a lower mean error than g01-03 (below 0.469), because harmonic averaging suppresses peers with temporarily depressed EBITDA.
compact: EV/EBITDA | rank sales_growth_1y 2, ebitda_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, roic 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=25, harmonic_mean, min_peers=3
critic_reason: The only new idea is the harmonic-mean aggregator; the features are a reshuffle of already-tried cross-industry driver rankings (g01-03, g02-05) with no new feature or screen, and the mechanism never explains why growth-matched peers from other industries should share a multiple, so this counts as an aggregator-only variant.
reason: critic: The only new idea is the harmonic-mean aggregator; the features are a reshuffle of already-tried cross-industry driver rankings (g01-03, g02-05) with no new feature or screen, and the mechanism never explains why growth-matched peers from other industries should share a multiple, so this counts as an aggregator-only variant.

name: roic_turnover_decomposition_sales
mechanism: EV/Sales factors exactly into EV/Invested capital times Invested capital/Sales; the first factor is set by ROIC relative to the cost of capital and by growth, the second by capital intensity (inverse asset turnover). Banding on ROIC fixes the value-creation spread across industries, and ranking on asset turnover, growth and EBIT margin matches the capital-intensity and growth terms, so peers share both factors of the sales multiple.
prediction: Beats the EV/Sales industry median in all 4 years with median error below 0.45.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band roic±0.04 | rank asset_turnover 2, sales_growth_1y 1, ebit_margin 1 | k=12, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band roic±0.08] -> []
critic_reason: The exact split of EV/Sales into EV/invested capital times invested capital/sales gives a specific mechanism, banding on ROIC is a new screen, ranking on asset turnover (with EBIT margin and growth) matches the capital-intensity and growth terms, and the all-4-years error claim is falsifiable.

name: gross_and_ebitda_margin_box_sales
mechanism: The gap between gross margin and EBITDA margin is operating-expense intensity (SG&A plus R&D), which separates firms that are scaling toward a high margin ceiling (high gross, low EBITDA margin, valued on future margins) from mature firms already at their ceiling. A joint band on gross and EBITDA margin matches both the business-model ceiling and the current cash conversion of sales, and ranking on growth, R&D and capex intensity matches the speed and cost of moving toward that ceiling.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years and achieves median error at or below 0.38, improving on g02-06 by matching current margin directly.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band gross_margin±0.06, band ebitda_margin±0.04 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 1, capex_intensity 1, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08] -> []
critic_reason: This mostly recombines tried recipes: g01-05 already bands EBITDA margin and ranks on gross margin, growth, capex and size, and g02-06 already bands gross margin; moving gross margin from a ranking feature into a band and copying g03-04's fallback (which drops the gross-margin band straight away) adds no real new economic idea.
reason: critic: This mostly recombines tried recipes: g01-05 already bands EBITDA margin and ranks on gross margin, growth, capex and size, and g02-06 already bands gross margin; moving gross margin from a ranking feature into a band and copying g03-04's fallback (which drops the gross-margin band straight away) adds no real new economic idea.

name: size_adjusted_margin_sales
mechanism: A dollar of EBITDA margin is capitalized at a rate that depends on its durability and the firm's discount rate, and large firms have more stable margins, better access to capital and lower required returns, so they trade at higher EV/Sales than small firms with the same margin. Jointly banding on EBITDA margin and sales size makes peers share both the cash margin and its capitalization rate, while ranking on growth, gross margin and R&D intensity matches pricing power and expensed intangible investment.
prediction: Beats the industry median in all 4 years with median error below 0.40, and lowers error relative to g01-05 mainly for firms in the bottom size quintile.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.03, band log_sales±1 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, rnd_intensity 1 | k=12, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.03] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.06] -> []
critic_reason: This is essentially g01-05 (EBITDA margin band ±0.03, ranking on growth and gross margin, which already includes size as a ranking feature) with size moved from a ranking feature into a band and capex swapped for R&D, and its first fallback falls back to g01-05's exact screen, so it is a trivial variant rather than a new mechanism.
reason: critic: This is essentially g01-05 (EBITDA margin band ±0.03, ranking on growth and gross margin, which already includes size as a ranking feature) with size moved from a ranking feature into a band and capex swapped for R&D, and its first fallback falls back to g01-05's exact screen, so it is a trivial variant rather than a new mechanism.

name: g05-01 EBITDA operating-leverage band
mechanism: A firm's EBITDA margin measures its operating leverage: at a 5% margin a 1% change in sales moves EBITDA by many percent, so its EBITDA is a noisy, often temporarily depressed denominator and the market capitalizes it at a higher, more volatile multiple than a 40%-margin firm's stable EBITDA. A hard EBITDA-margin band across industries groups firms whose denominators share the same noise and mean-reversion profile, and ranking on EBIT margin (D&A intensity), ROIC, growth, R&D and size matches the remaining numerator drivers.
prediction: EV/EBITDA median error below the industry median baseline (0.333) and beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years, with coverage of at least 99%.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen band ebitda_margin±0.05 | rank ebit_margin 1, roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 0.5, log_assets 0.5 | k=15, trimmed_mean, min_peers=8 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.1] -> []
critic_reason: Using an EBITDA-margin band as the hard screen for EV/EBITDA has not been tried (earlier margin bands were all for EV/Sales). The idea that thin-margin firms have a noisy, mean-reverting denominator that the market capitalizes at a higher multiple is specific and falsifiable, and the cross-industry band plus D&A/ROIC/growth ranking does what the mechanism says.

name: g05-02 Sector plus lender-revealed durability
mechanism: The 2-digit sector sets the base cost of capital and cyclicality, but within a sector lenders still distinguish firms with contracted or recurring EBITDA (which they lend 4-5x against) from firms with fragile EBITDA (lent 1-2x or nothing), so net debt/EBITDA is an accounting-revealed measure of within-sector cash-flow durability. Requiring peers from the same sector AND a similar leverage multiple matches both the sector discount rate and the within-sector durability of the denominator, and ranking on EBITDA and EBIT margins, ROIC and growth matches the remaining drivers.
prediction: EV/EBITDA median error at or below 0.325 and beats the industry median in all 4 years.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band net_debt_to_ebitda±1.5 | rank ebitda_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, roic 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=10, trimmed_mean, min_peers=6 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: A net-debt/EBITDA band inside the 2-digit sector is a new screen combination, not a k, weight or aggregator tweak. It matches both the observed proxy for durability and the net-debt part of EV/EBITDA, which is allowed accounting data. Note that leverage is partly a choice: net-cash firms with durable EBITDA will be grouped with firms lenders avoid, so a failure would point to that confound.

name: g05-03 Sector plus capital-structure (trade-off theory)
mechanism: Enterprise value includes the capitalized value of debt tax shields minus expected distress costs, both of which scale with book leverage, so two firms with identical operating drivers but different debt/assets carry different EV/EBITDA. Banding on debt/assets inside the 2-digit sector matches the tax-shield and distress component, and ranking on net margin alongside EBITDA and EBIT margins captures the interest-and-tax wedge between operating and bottom-line profit that signals how close a firm is to financial distress.
prediction: Beats the industry median in at least 3 of 4 years with EV/EBITDA median error below 0.333 and mean error below 0.50.
compact: EV/EBITDA | screen same industry_l2, band debt_to_assets±0.1 | rank ebitda_margin 1, ebit_margin 1, net_margin 1, sales_growth_1y 1 | k=12, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [same industry_l2] -> []
critic_reason: A book-leverage band inside the sector is a new screen with a specific trade-off-theory reason (tax shields minus distress costs, plus the known negative link between leverage and growth options). Adding net margin to the ranking puts the interest-and-tax wedge into practice. The effect may be second-order next to operating drivers, but the test is falsifiable.

name: g05-04 Sales multiple = margin x lender-revealed durability
mechanism: EV/Sales factors into EBITDA margin times EV/EBITDA; the margin band fixes the first factor, and the second factor depends on how durable that EBITDA is, which lenders reveal through how many turns of EBITDA they are willing to lend (net debt/EBITDA). Jointly banding on both matches the two factors across industries, with growth, gross margin, R&D and size matching remaining capitalization drivers, and fallbacks that relax the leverage screen first because margin matters most.
prediction: EV/Sales median error below 0.40 with 100% coverage and beats the industry median in all 4 years.

spec.name: g05-04 Sales multiple = margin x lender-revealed durability

compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.04, band net_debt_to_ebitda±1.5 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, gross_margin 1, rnd_intensity 0.5, log_sales 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08] -> []
critic_reason: In the EV/Sales universe many targets have near-zero or negative EBITDA. For them net debt/EBITDA blows up or flips sign and says nothing about how many turns lenders would lend, so the leverage band only works for firms where EV/EBITDA would be used anyway. It is also a fourth 'EBITDA-margin band plus one more band' variant (after g03-04, g04-05 and g04-06), with a second screen that does not fit the multiple.

name: g05-05 Asset-turnover class with Tobin's-Q drivers
mechanism: EV/Sales factors exactly into EV/Assets times Assets/Sales; a hard band on asset turnover fixes the second factor (the business model's asset intensity, e.g. distributor vs. manufacturer vs. software). The first factor, a Tobin's-Q-like ratio, is driven by the return earned on assets (EBITDA margin given turnover), growth, and unrecorded intangible assets proxied by R&D intensity, so ranking heavily on margin plus growth and R&D matches it.
prediction: EV/Sales median error below 0.45 with 100% coverage and beats the industry median in all 4 years.

spec.name: g05-05 Asset-turnover class with Tobin's-Q drivers

compact: EV/Sales | screen band asset_turnover±0.2 | rank ebitda_margin 3, sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 1 | k=12, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band asset_turnover±0.4] -> []
critic_reason: Splitting EV/Sales exactly into EV/Assets times Assets/Sales, banding on turnover and ranking on Q drivers, is a new and clearly stated idea, and the recipe matches it. However, a fixed ±0.2 raw band barely fixes Assets/Sales for low-turnover targets (0.3 lets in 0.1 to 0.5, i.e. 2x to 10x assets/sales), so expect the largest errors in capital-heavy firms.

name: g05-06 Pre-tax free-cash margin match
mechanism: What a dollar of sales is worth is the free cash it produces, and before working capital and taxes that is EBITDA margin minus capex intensity; two firms with the same EBITDA margin but different capex needs convert very different shares of sales into distributable cash. Jointly banding EBITDA margin and capex intensity pins down this pre-tax free-cash margin across industries, and ranking on growth, R&D intensity and ROIC matches the growth-dependent capitalization factor and expensed intangible investment.
prediction: EV/Sales median error below 0.42 with 100% coverage and beats the industry median in all 4 years.
compact: EV/Sales | screen band ebitda_margin±0.04, band capex_intensity±0.03 | rank sales_growth_1y 1, rnd_intensity 1, roic 0.5 | k=10, median, min_peers=6 | fallback [band ebitda_margin±0.04] -> [band ebitda_margin±0.08] -> []
critic_reason: Making capex intensity a hard band next to EBITDA margin directly matches the pre-tax free-cash margin (EBITDA margin minus capex/sales). That is a sharper and economically different constraint from earlier recipes, which only gave capex a soft rank weight, and the prediction is falsifiable.
